title: 4|n law is a small-n (n<=12) artifact: rule30 dominates asymptotically
question: Does H_337's 4|n law (4|n <=> rule30 dominant) hold at n in {14,16,20}? Predictions: n=14 rule110, n=16 rule30, n=20 rule30.
engine: pure hexa-lang. ECA periodic ring, Floyd period detection (memory-free), sampled starts (stride 16/64/1024 for n=14/16/20).

falsifier_eval.F340_1_ALL_PREDICTIONS_MATCH: FAIL — 2/3 match; n=14 (4-not-div) predicted rule110 but rule30 dominates (1219 vs 43)
falsifier_eval.F340_2_4N_LAW_UNIVERSAL: FAIL — the 4|n law does NOT extend past n=12; rule30 wins at n=14 despite 4-not-div
falsifier_eval.F340_3_RULE30_ASYMPTOTIC_DOMINANCE: PASS (emergent) — rule30 cycle length explodes with n (1219@14, 4605@16, 4222@20) while rule110 stays small (31-98), so rule30 dominates ALL n>=14 regardless of 4-divisibility
falsifier_eval.F340_4_DETERMINISTIC: PASS — Floyd period detection, fixed sampling stride

verdict_derived: 🔴 FALSIFIED — the 4|n law (H_337) is a SMALL-N (n<=12) artifact, not a universal number-theory law. At n>=14, rule30 (chaotic class III) dominates the longest-cycle slot unconditionally: its mean cycle length explodes (1219 at n=14, 4605 at n=16) as the chaotic orbit fills exponentially more of the state space, while rule110's mean stays bounded (31-98). The n=4->n=12 oscillation between rule30 and rule110 is therefore a finite-size effect: at small n, rule30's chaotic cycles are short enough that rule110's universal structure can win at the 4-not-div sizes (6,10), but this crossover vanishes once n is large enough for chaos to express. This is an honest closed-negative that REFINES H_337: the 4|n pattern is real but bounded to n<=12.
structural_vs_dynamical: DYNAMICAL kernel at large scale (up to 2^20 states, sampled). The discovery is a regime boundary: number-theoretic control of dominance (4|n) only operates while chaotic cycle length is sub-saturating; beyond n~12 raw chaotic expansion dominates.
honest_limits: Sampled starts (1024 per n via stride); the rule30 lead (>10x) is far beyond sampling noise, but a full sweep at n=14 would remove the caveat
Floyd cap 8192; rule30 cycles at n=20 may exceed (capped to -1 and excluded), slightly underestimating r30 — but it already dominates by 40x so the verdict is robust
Three n only; the exact crossover (does it vanish at n=13 or n=14?) is not pinned — n=13 (prime, odd ring) is a separate parity class
Two rules; other chaotic rules may have different saturation onsets
